summary: Locked batched requests and stalled GPU fences in dedicated eu-west pool during midday window
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 11:40 - 12:15 UTC we observed a sustained p50/p99 throughput degradation for LexiOps' dedicated capacity in eu-west. Multiple GPU attachments in the reserved pool reported long-running fence waits and batch queues stalled, causing requests to pile up and autoscaler to fail to reclaim or reassign slots. Impact: customer saw increased tail latency and ~30% reduction in overall throughput for API routes pinned to rwkv-14b. This affected production traffic during the customer's peak window and triggered customer alerts.

Timeline: 
- 11:38 UTC: LexiOps reported elevated p99 latency to Support via email.
- 11:40 UTC: Internal alerts from serving-runtime and scheduler (queue depth spike) start firing.
- 11:43 UTC: Autoscaler attempted to attach an extra GPU but allocation hung waiting on fence clear.
- 11:50 UTC: Support engaged SRE/Eng; mitigation applied (traffic diversion to fallback pool).
- 12:05 UTC: Some batches resumed after manual eviction of two suspect tenants; partial throughput recovery.

Observed behavior: 
- Repeated kernel/driver warnings referencing fence timeouts and stalled NVLink transfers for GPU UUIDs GPU-3a5f and GPU-7b12.
- Scheduling logs show many short-lived stream attachments from a high-churn tenant (tenant_id: lexio-tn-338) creating many tiny batches that serialized on the kernel fence.
- Autoscaler did not reclaim stalled slots within expected 20s window; slot state remained "ATTACHED_LOCKED" and subsequent attach requests blocked behind the locked resources.

Expected behavior: 
- Short streams should be multiplexed without causing persistent fence locks and autoscaler should be able to detach and reattach GPUs within configured window to restore throughput.

Business impact: Customer reported failed in-app requests during peak; revenue-impacting for LexiOps' scheduled demo.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Reserve a dedicated pool with mixed long- and short-stream tenants in eu-west (replicate similar tenant churn profile).
2) Generate high-frequency tiny streams (10-50 token requests, <200ms between requests) from one tenant while another tenant sends medium-sized batches (512-1024 tokens).
3) Observe scheduler and GPU attach/detach logs; look for fence timeouts and ATTACHED_LOCKED state transitions.
4) Trigger autoscaler by briefly increasing load to force allocation; observe blocked attach requests behind locked slots.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses: (1) Noisy short-stream tenant creates frequent kernel primitives that leave fence objects in non-signaled state, causing NVLink transfers to stall; (2) GPU driver/firmware bug exacerbated by mixed batch sizes and high-ephemeral-stream churn; (3) Autoscaler logic treats ATTACHED_LOCKED as attach-in-progress and does not trigger forced eviction quickly enough.
Initial findings: 
- Grafana: queue_depth and gpu_fence_wait_time correlate to lexio-tn-338 traffic spikes (links: https://grafana.redwood/in/dedicated/pool-eu-west?from=2026-03-12T11:30&to=2026-03-12T12:30).
- Kernel traces: nvlink-retry counters spike on GPU-3a5f.
- Tenant metrics: lexio-tn-338 had >8000 short streams in 30m window, median request size 42 tokens.
Actions taken: diverted ~25% of LexiOps traffic to fallback shared tier to buy time; performed manual eviction on two slots to recover partial capacity.
Next steps: collect full kernel traces from affected hosts, reproduce in staging with synthetic churn workload, patch autoscaler to detect ATTACHED_LOCKED > 45s as eviction candidate, coordinate with driver team for possible firmware/driver update.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported high p99 at 11:38 UTC, created this ticket and escalated to SRE.
SRE (Jonah): Observed fence timeouts on two GPUs and blocked attach requests. Temporarily diverted traffic; requesting kernel traces from affected hosts (host ids: host-eu-021, host-eu-022).
Customer (LexiOps PM): Confirmed heavy short-stream traffic started after a new client-side retry loop was deployed at 11:20 UTC. Can throttle that tenant if recommended.
Eng (Marta Chen): Hypothesis: autoscaler state machine needs to treat ATTACHED_LOCKED as a failed attach after threshold. Draft PR created to add eviction timeout.
SRE (Jonah): Mitigation applied at 11:50 UTC (traffic diversion + manual evictions). Partial recovery observed by 12:05 UTC. Monitoring for re-occurrence.
resolution: Mitigations in-place: isolated noisy tenant via placement tag, diverted portion of traffic to fallback tier, manual eviction of two stuck slots, and increased autoscaler eviction timeout to 45s as temporary safety net. Engineering will land autoscaler state fix (PR cited) and SRE will coordinate driver/firmware validation with vendor. Pending: driver patch validation, staged reproduction in infra-staging, and permanent scheduler hardening.
